To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of sperm morphologies in the dead and live populations of an eosine stained dry film are different and that assessment of the functional spermatozo in an ejaculate is made by reference to normal oval forms in live population.

the distribution of sperm morphology in the vital population of spermatozoal differs from that of the dead population, and that normal oval spermatozoal appear preferentially in the former population.
the percentage of normal, oval forms in a live population is a more reliable indicator of the functional status of an ejaculate than the total number of spermatozoas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spermatozoa of 80 men.
the morphology of spermatozoan and the relationship between the morphology of sperm and fertility.
the development of a new method for assessing the total number of viable and functional spermatozoas in a semen sample.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the percentage of normal sperm forms in the live group of a dry smear of an ejaculate is an accurate and reliable indicator of the functional capacity of the spermatozoa.
the spermatozoa are the only cells that can be used as a source of DNA for the purpose of genetic analysis.
the percentage of oval forms in the vital population provides an accurate and reproducible measure of the total number and functional status of spermatozo in an ejaculate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are no morphological characteristics that are unique for live or dead spermatozoa.
the spermatozoal population is not a static population.
the morphology of the spermatozoa should be assessed by the use of an eosin stained dry film and the percentage of normal spermatozoa determined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are differences in morphology between the dead and vital population of spermatozoan.
the use of the dry film technique to assess human spermatozoal morphology is valid and that this method is suitable for the routine assessment of human sperm morphology.
the morphology assessment of human spermatozoal populations is an important parameter to consider in the diagnosis of infertility.
